about.lead: I am a data scientist and a Full Stack developer.
body: I use Python, SQL, exploratory analysis, statistics and Machine Learning on concrete business problems.
I frame ambiguous needs with BI, business and technical teams, then turn them into measurable solutions.
I also ship web applications with React, Node.js, Express and REST APIs.
I work with Git, tests and clear documentation. I explain results to non-technical stakeholders.
I speak fluent French and professional English.

experiences.oneLiner: I connected a business need to Python data processing, PostgreSQL and a web application.
experiences.context: I was expected to turn concrete needs into reliable data pipelines and to contribute to a management web application.
solo: I turned concrete problems into automated data processing in Python.
I extracted, cleaned, transformed and validated data from online sources before integration.
I loaded the processed data into a PostgreSQL database.
I built features for a management web app with React, Node.js, Express.js and a REST API, using tests and sound coding practices.
I documented the data processing I delivered.
collab: I framed requirements with business teams.
I contributed to data quality and consistency reviews.

experiences.context: I was expected to understand needs, design solutions, implement them and keep quality under control.
solo: I designed software solutions from analyzed business needs.
I developed and maintained software features.
I ran functional and technical tests.
I diagnosed and fixed technical defects.
collab: I analyzed business needs and designed solutions with stakeholders.
I communicated results to the relevant teams.

projects.title: Student performance and success analysis
cardLines: I explored academic data with Python, Pandas and Scikit-learn.
I looked for success factors and student profiles.
I made the findings readable for non-specialists.
projects.impact: This project shows I can turn raw data into profiles useful for teachers or managers.
projects.glance: I analyzed academic data to identify success factors and student profiles.
projects.context: The question was what supports student success. That helps target support more clearly.
projects.data: The data were academic records. They describe student pathways and outcomes.
approach: I cleaned and prepared the data for analysis.
I ran exploratory data analysis (EDA). EDA summarizes and visualizes data to understand it.
I applied statistical methods and Machine Learning with Scikit-learn.
I summarized factors and profiles in plain language.
methods: Exploratory analysis reveals patterns before modeling.
Machine learning models help group or classify profiles from the data.
I chose these methods to move from raw detail to a readable summary.
deliverables: A synthesis of factors and profiles
demonstrates: Applied EDA, statistics and Machine Learning
improvements: Compare other models based on the business need

projects.title: Anomaly detection in data
cardLines: I looked for unusual observations in data.
I combined a statistical approach with an algorithmic approach.
The goal was to improve reliability before any decision.
projects.impact: This project shows I can flag suspicious data before it leads to a poor decision.
projects.glance: I detected anomalies to improve data reliability.
projects.context: An anomaly is an unusual observation. Finding it avoids decisions based on misleading data.
projects.data: The dataset included observations that needed review. Some could differ strongly from the rest.
approach: I prepared the data for detection.
I applied a statistical method to flag unusual gaps.
I applied an algorithmic method to catch other atypical cases.
I compared both approaches to focus attention where it matters.
methods: A statistical approach compares each point to the overall distribution.
An algorithmic approach learns patterns and flags what differs.
Combining them reduces missed cases and noisy alerts.
deliverables: A list of observations to review
demonstrates: Careful use of statistical and algorithmic methods

projects.title: Vector search and data analysis
cardLines: I generated embeddings with Sentence Transformers.
An embedding turns text into a sequence of numbers that represents meaning.
I stored those representations in MongoDB Atlas for similarity search.
projects.impact: This project shows I can move from keyword search to meaning-based search.
projects.glance: I built similarity search from text embeddings.
projects.context: Keyword search often misses texts with similar meaning. Similarity search compares meaning instead.
projects.data: The data were texts to index and compare with each other.
approach: I prepared the texts for analysis.
I generated embeddings with Sentence Transformers.
I stored the vectors in MongoDB Atlas.
I queried the database by similarity to retrieve close texts.
methods: Sentence Transformers produce a numeric representation of a sentence's meaning.
Similarity search compares those representations to find the closest ones.
MongoDB Atlas stores the vectors and supports related queries.
demonstrates: Storage and search with MongoDB Atlas
improvements: Evaluate result quality with annotated examples
Try other embedding models based on the language of the texts

projects.title: Management application (Full Stack case study)
cardLines: This case study is based only on my internship at Network Pro Service.
I processed data in Python and loaded it into PostgreSQL.
I built web features with React, Node.js, Express and a REST API.
projects.impact: This case study shows I can deliver the full path from need to data to application.
projects.glance: I contributed to a management app connected to data processing and PostgreSQL.
projects.context: The need was to make data reliable and usable inside a management application.
projects.data: The data came from online sources. I cleaned and validated them before integration.
approach: I framed requirements with business teams.
I automated extraction, cleaning and validation in Python.
I loaded the data into PostgreSQL.
I built front-end and back-end features with tests and documentation.
methods: React, Node.js, Express and a REST API expose features to users.
demonstrates: Combined data and Full Stack delivery
Work with tests, documentation and business framing
improvements: Expand test coverage as features grow
